name: Review Fleet Work and Improve
description: Operator-triggered improvement loop. Given an operator's description of something they just tried with the fleet, find the relevant recent missions, review what happened from the work tree, classify shortcomings into the 9-module tiered set, execute the improvements (REPO via scan+PR, LOCAL via Firestore/overlay), and report back.

request.description: The operator's description of what they tried and what to improve

target_agent.description: Which fleet agent/team to review, if named (e.g. dot, archie)

lookback_hours.description: How far back to search for the relevant missions

steps.title: Find the work to review
steps.description: The operator described something they just tried: ${request}. Using work-management, run work-log-read for the relevant window (--hours ${lookback_hours}; add --owner ${target_agent} if an agent was named). Identify the specific mission(s) that match the operator's description. If several match, pick the most recent that fits; if none clearly match, ask the operator to clarify which attempt they mean (needs_input).
steps.accept_criteria: The matching mission(s) identified by work ID, with a one-line summary of what each tried to do. If ambiguous, a clarifying question was asked instead of guessing.

steps.title: Review what happened (evidence from the work tree)
steps.description: ⚠️ READ-ONLY STEP. For each identified mission, read the full work tree via work-management (work-log-read / the mission tree). Derive the evidence DIRECTLY from the tree — do NOT rely on aggregated metrics that may not exist. Capture: total envelopes (M/C/T), failed or retried tasks, cortex re-plans (a checkpoint re-issued after a failure), delegation handoffs and their round-trip counts, any ENOENT/permission/access errors, time from start to finish, and where the mission stalled or produced a poor result. Optionally cross-reference brain-telemetry-read for dispatch failures on the same window.
steps.accept_criteria: A concrete assessment: what went wrong or was suboptimal, with specific evidence (envelope counts, failure points, round-trips, durations) cited from the work tree — not from assumed telemetry.

steps.title: Classify and improve
steps.description: Map the assessment to one or more of the 9 improvement modules (read the architect-prime project context for module definitions). REPO modules (7): p-improve-daemons, p-improve-souls, p-improve-gateway, p-improve-skills, p-improve-dashboard, p-improve-context-repo, p-improve-work-layer-repo. LOCAL modules (2): p-improve-context-local, p-improve-work-layer-local. Delegation is not a module — route delegation findings to the owning module (governance → daemons, instruction quality → souls, process steps → work-layer-repo or -local, operator patterns → context-local). For each module, follow its improvement process. REPO improvements land via the repo-improvement skill (contamination scan + PR). LOCAL improvements land via the local-improvement skill (Firestore/overlay, no PR). Keep each module's changes separate (one module per commit). A single finding never mixes tiers.
steps.accept_criteria: At least one module's improvement executed with before/after reasoning. REPO changes via PR, LOCAL changes via Firestore/overlay. Changes scoped one-module-per-commit.

steps.title: Submit changes
steps.description: For REPO changes: land per the repo-improvement skill — contamination scan, branch, PR to main with module, evidence, and expected effect. For LOCAL changes: land per the local-improvement skill — Firestore write or operator/ overlay, no PR. Record all document paths and PR links.
steps.accept_criteria: PR link provided for REPO changes, OR Firestore document path(s) for LOCAL changes. Each improvement has exactly one landing type.

steps.title: Report back to the operator
steps.description: Reply in the operator's chat thread (the same dashboard conversation that triggered this). Summarize: which mission was reviewed, what was found (in plain language — the operator is not reading the work tree), what was improved (noting tier: upstream PR or local persist), the PR link or Firestore change, and what the operator should expect to see differently next time. Keep it concise and non-technical.
steps.accept_criteria: A clear, concise summary delivered to the originating dashboard chat thread, understandable without opening the PR.
